title: China's party envoy in Dhaka cites Teesta and Mongla projects, invites BNP to Beijing
dek: Liu Haixing told Prime Minister Tarique Rahman that China backs Bangladesh joining the RCEP trade bloc. At a separate roundtable he said work on two projects close to India is moving steadily: the Teesta river plan and the Mongla port industrial park.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
A senior Chinese Communist Party official used a three-day visit to Dhaka to press for closer political and economic ties with Bangladesh's new government. Liu Haixing told a roundtable on Wednesday that work on two Chinese-backed projects near India is "advancing steadily": a plan to dredge and embank the Teesta river, and an industrial park at Mongla port.

Liu, who heads the International Department of the party's Central Committee, met Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Secretariat on Wednesday afternoon. According to Rahman's office, he said China supports Bangladesh joining the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), the Asia-Pacific trade bloc that India left in 2019. He also invited a delegation of Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), led by its secretary general, to visit China.

## What happened

Liu arrived in Dhaka on Tuesday night for a visit running from 3 to 5 November, The Business Standard (TBS) reported. He was also scheduled to meet President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir. According to bdnews24.com, he laid wreaths at the graves of the BNP's founder, Ziaur Rahman, and former prime minister Khaleda Zia.

His meeting with the prime minister began at about 1.20 pm local time, according to the state news agency BSS, as carried by TBS. Rahman's deputy press secretary, Shahadat Shadhin, briefed reporters afterwards. He said Rahman asked for China's help in resolving the Rohingya crisis. Bangladesh shelters about 1.3 million Rohingya refugees from Myanmar, and Rahman said they put heavy economic, social, demographic and environmental pressure on the country. Liu replied that China was aware of the crisis and would convey the prime minister's concerns to President Xi Jinping.

The two sides also discussed the Bangladesh-China-Myanmar economic corridor and closer ties between the Chinese Communist Party and the BNP, the briefing said. Liu said China's commitment to Bangladesh's development was unchanged. Bangladesh's State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Shama Obaed Islam, attended, as did Peng Xiubin, who heads the Chinese party department's bureau for South-East and South Asian affairs.

Earlier on Wednesday, Liu gave the keynote speech at a roundtable organised by the Chinese Embassy in a Dhaka hotel. The event also opened a new "Bangladesh-China Centre for Party and State Governance Studies". According to Prothom Alo and TBS, he said:

- work is advancing steadily on the Mongla Port Industrial Park and on the "comprehensive treatment and restoration of the Teesta River"
- trade between the two countries has grown from about $15 million to more than $23 billion over five decades
- Bangladesh was the first South Asian country to sign a Belt and Road cooperation memorandum with China
- China is willing to import more Bangladeshi products

> "We do not draw ideological lines, nor distinguish friends based on whether a party is in or out of government." Liu Haixing, as reported by Prothom Alo

Liu said his department keeps up ties with 816 political parties and 18 political organisations in 173 countries.

## Background

The visit builds on Rahman's official visit to China from 22 to 26 June, when he met Xi Jinping. The joint communiqué from that visit, dated 26 June, names both projects Liu mentioned: the "Teesta River Comprehensive Management and Restoration Project" and the "Mongla Port Facilities Modernization and Expansion Project". In the same document, Bangladesh "resolutely opposed any form of 'Taiwan independence'".

The Teesta project matters most for India and for north Bengal. The river rises in Sikkim and crosses Jalpaiguri district before entering Bangladesh. India and Bangladesh have never signed a deal on sharing its water. The draft agreement prepared in 2011 was dropped after objections from West Bengal's chief minister at the time.

Bangladesh has turned to China instead. In August 2025, Prothom Alo reported that Bangladesh had asked China for a loan of Tk 67 billion, about $550 million, towards a first phase costing $750 million. The feasibility study was done by the state-owned Power Construction Corporation of China (PowerChina). According to that report, the plan covers:

- dredging 102 km of the river to a depth of about 10 metres
- 203 km of embankments
- reclaiming about 171 sq km of land
- police stations, coast guard outposts and army camps along the river

Work was then scheduled to run from 2026 to 2029. A security analyst quoted in the same report said India would oppose a Chinese-funded project so close to the Siliguri Corridor. This narrow strip of land in north Bengal links the north-eastern states to the rest of India. Prothom Alo also noted that India had earlier shown interest in financing the river's restoration itself. The Declaration could not confirm whether a Chinese loan agreement for the Teesta has since been signed.

Mongla, Bangladesh's second-largest seaport, is on the Pasur river near the Sundarbans, a short distance from the West Bengal border.

## What it means for India

The visit shows China building ties with Bangladesh through the ruling party as well as through the government. Liu's department, which handles the Chinese party's relations with foreign parties, is working the same way elsewhere in South Asia: on Monday he met Pakistan's army chief and foreign minister in Rawalpindi and Islamabad.

For India, the risks are concrete. China would gain a role in managing a river that India shares with Bangladesh, close to the Siliguri Corridor. Chinese-built port infrastructure would stand near the Bengal border. And Dhaka would gain a path into a trade bloc that India has stayed out of. These moves come at a delicate time. The 1996 Ganges water-sharing treaty between India and Bangladesh expires on 12 December, and there is no automatic extension clause, AFP reported last week. India's foreign ministry said last week that it wants "constructive" ties with Dhaka but had not set a date for talks on renewing the treaty.

Neither the prime minister's office nor the reports of Liu's speech mentioned India.

## What happens next

Liu's visit ends on Thursday. No date has been announced for the BNP delegation's trip to China. Bangladesh's bid to join the RCEP will need the agreement of the bloc's existing members, which include China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand and the ten ASEAN states. The Ganges treaty deadline of 12 December is the next fixed point in India-Bangladesh relations.
